report.summary: (model supplied no summary; its answer is preserved in handoff)

handoff.purpose: Render a council deliberation as markdown, with explicit ordering and quorum honesty.

symbols.name: _turns_of
symbols.note: Normalizes a transcript into a list of turns; handles None, Mapping, list/tuple, and object/dict with turns/records/entries fields.

symbols.name: _chain_head
symbols.note: Returns the chain head digest from transcript or verdict, falling back to the last turn's entry_sha.

symbols.name: _quorum_counts
symbols.note: Returns (answered, requested, answered_vendors, missing_vendors); derives counts from vendor lists when present, else from integer fields.

symbols.name: _evidence_paths
symbols.note: Collects evidence path strings from verdict evidence and paths fields.

symbols.name: render_markdown
symbols.note: Renders a council verdict and transcript to markdown with a deliberate order: outcome, advisory banner, quorum honesty, dissents, convergence, evidence, cost/latency, deliberation, and provenance footer. Pure function with no I/O or network.

claims.text: Order is deliberate and load-bearing: outcome and the quorum honesty line lead, so a degraded council is the first thing a reader sees and cannot be skimmed past.
claims.why: Lines 330-335 append outcome and quorum honesty immediately after the header, before any other content.

claims.text: Then EVERY dissent verbatim with its author -- BEFORE the convergence, because the dissent is the only part that could not have come from asking one model twice.
claims.why: Lines 354-373 render dissents (including verbatim text) before the convergence section starting at line 375.

claims.text: Then where the vendors converged, evidence digests, per-vendor cost/latency, the deliberation itself, and finally the provenance footer (bus path + chain head) that lets a reader verify all of it offline.
claims.why: Sections appear in order: convergence (375), evidence (384), cost/latency (397), deliberation (412), provenance footer (430+).

claims.text: Pure: no I/O, no network, no gate.
claims.why: The function only builds strings and calls local helpers; no imports or calls that would do I/O, network, or gate operations appear in this chunk.

claims.text: The advisory banner is UNCONDITIONAL. A verdict arriving without the marker is a contract violation, so we say so instead of quietly rendering it as if it carried authority.
claims.why: Lines 327-334 unconditionally append the advisory banner and, when advisory is not True, append a caution block explaining the violation.

claims.text: Quorum honesty, at the top. A short council is a weaker signal and that must be impossible to miss -- it is a warning block, not a footnote.
claims.why: Lines 337-345 append a WARNING block when answered < requested, and the block appears before the dissents and convergence sections.

claims.text: DISSENT LEADS. Not a stylistic choice: the dissent is the only content in this document that could not have been produced by asking one model twice.
claims.why: The dissents section is appended before the convergence section; no other content that could be produced by one model appears between outcome and dissents except the quorum honesty line.

claims.text: A vendor that did not speak has no content; an empty fence is noise that makes a silent turn look like an empty answer.
claims.why: Line 372 checks `if text:` before appending the verbatim fence, so empty text produces no fence.

claims.text: Convergence is an OBSERVATION about what these vendors said, not a decision and not a vote. Models with overlapping training data agreeing is not independent confirmation, and nothing here counts as a passed gate.
claims.why: Lines 380-382 append the explanatory text; the code never uses the word 'majority' except as a legacy alias in _field and the rendered text explicitly disclaims decision/vote/gate.

claims.text: A turn that did not SPEAK is the quorum honesty story at turn level: bus.py records "refused" / "unavailable" / "budget_exhausted" / "anomaly" rather than dropping the vendor, so rendering the status is the difference between "three vendors agreed" and "one was never asked".
claims.why: Lines 421-426 read the turn status and, when status is not empty and not 'spoke', append a NOTE block with the status and reason.

claims.text: Paths an egress lane declined to send are NAMED, not counted -- a vendor reasoning over less evidence than the others is not an equal voice, and hiding that would make the roster look stronger than it was.
claims.why: Lines 428-433 read the withheld list and append a NOTE block listing each withheld path by name.

claims.text: Where the canonical record lives. Explicit field wins; otherwise derived from the council id, which is how bus.py names the file.
claims.where: _bus_path docstring (function not shown in this chunk)
claims.why: The _bus_path function body is not in this chunk; only its docstring appears at the top of the chunk.

claims.text: The chain head digest a reader verifies the bus against. Explicit field wins; otherwise the last turn's entry_sha, which IS the head by construction in an append-only chain.
claims.why: Lines 294-301 check transcript fields, then verdict fields, then the last turn's entry_sha/sha/digest, exactly as described.

claims.text: Counts are derived from the vendor LISTS when present, because a list is checkable against the transcript and a bare integer is not.
claims.why: Lines 305-309 extract vendor lists; lines 312-314 use integer fields only when the integer is an int, otherwise fall back to list lengths.

claims.text: A transcript may be the turn list itself, or an object/dict carrying one.
claims.why: Lines 284-291 handle None, Mapping, list/tuple, and object/dict with turns/records/entries fields.

claims.text: Paths named by the evidence, for the path-marker half of the floor.
claims.why: Lines 319-324 collect string/bytes items and label/path/file/name fields from evidence items, plus paths from the paths field.

observations.what: The _bus_path docstring appears at the start of this chunk, but the function body is not shown; the chunk begins mid-function with its docstring and body.
The _bus_path docstring is followed by its body in lines 284-292, but the function definition line is not visible in this chunk; the chunk starts with the docstring and body.

The render_markdown function references DEGRADED_QUORUM_MARKER, DEFAULT_BUS_DIR, _verbatim, _short, _field, _as_list, _text, _turns_of, _bus_path, _chain_head, and _quorum_counts; all are defined elsewhere in the file or in the same file as listed in the names defined elsewhere.
The quorum honesty warning uses a WARNING block with the DEGRADED_QUORUM_MARKER constant, but the constant's definition is not in this chunk.
The cost/latency table renders cost and latency as text via _text when present, but the _text function may not preserve numeric formatting; this is a rendering nuance but not a defect in this chunk.
